questions.question: Which S3 bucket receives the organization CloudTrail logs, and what is the AWS account ID of the account that owns it?
questions.answer: The organization trail hrl-org-trail delivers to the bucket hrl-org-cloudtrail-739204615882-use2 in the hrl-log-archive account, account ID 739204615882.

sources.passage: The trail delivers to the bucket hrl-org-cloudtrail-739204615882-use2 in the hrl-log-archive account (739204615882).

questions.question: How long are CloudTrail logs retained, and how are they tiered over time?
questions.answer: Logs are protected by S3 Object Lock in compliance mode for 400 days, then transitioned to S3 Glacier Deep Archive, and expired after 2,555 days (7 years).

sources.passage: The bucket uses S3 Object Lock in compliance mode with a 400-day retention period. Objects transition to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 400 days and are expired after 2,555 days (7 years)

questions.question: Which AWS Regions is HRL allowed to use, and what enforces the restriction?
questions.answer: Only us-east-2 (Ohio, primary) and us-west-2 (Oregon, disaster recovery). All other Regions are blocked by the SCP hrl-scp-deny-regions, with exemptions for global services.

sources.passage: The primary Region is us-east-2 (Ohio)
The disaster recovery Region is us-west-2 (Oregon). All other Regions are blocked by the SCP hrl-scp-deny-regions

questions.question: What are the lifetime and budget limits for sandbox accounts, and what happens when the budget is exceeded?
questions.answer: Sandbox accounts live at most 90 days with a monthly budget of USD 500. At 120 percent of budget the account is automatically moved to the Suspended OU.

sources.passage: Sandbox accounts have a maximum lifetime of 90 days and a monthly budget of USD 500. When actual spend reaches 120 percent of the sandbox budget the account is automatically moved to the Suspended OU.

questions.question: How does a team request a new AWS account and how long does vending take?
questions.answer: By opening a pull request to the hrl-aft-account-requests repository; Account Factory for Terraform (AFT) creates the account, with a service level of 2 business days from pull request approval.

sources.passage: New accounts are requested by pull request to the repository hrl-aft-account-requests.
The service level for account vending is 2 business days from pull request approval.

questions.question: What is the Amazon side ASN of the primary Transit Gateway and of the DR Transit Gateway?
questions.answer: The primary Transit Gateway hrl-tgw-use2-01 uses ASN 64620; the DR Transit Gateway hrl-tgw-usw2-01 uses ASN 64621.

sources.passage: The primary Transit Gateway hrl-tgw-use2-01 uses Amazon side ASN 64620 and the DR Transit Gateway hrl-tgw-usw2-01 uses Amazon side ASN 64621.

questions.question: Why is appliance mode enabled on the inspection VPC attachment?
questions.answer: Appliance mode pins both directions of a flow to the same Availability Zone firewall endpoint, which is required for symmetric routing; without it stateful inspection would drop return traffic.

sources.passage: Appliance mode keeps both directions of a flow pinned to the same Availability Zone firewall endpoint, which is required for symmetric routing; without it, stateful inspection drops return traffic.

questions.question: Describe HRL's AWS Direct Connect connections.
questions.answer: Two dedicated 10 Gbps connections: Colo Site A in Columbus (dxcon-fh41a7c2) and Colo Site B in Chicago (dxcon-fg92b8d3), both attached via transit VIFs to Direct Connect gateway hrl-dxgw-01 (ASN 64630).

sources.passage: HRL has two dedicated 10 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connections terminating at Colo Site A in Columbus (dxcon-fh41a7c2) and Colo Site B in Chicago (dxcon-fg92b8d3). Both connections attach to the Direct Connect gateway hrl-dxgw-01 (ASN 64630)

questions.question: How is Direct Connect kept preferred over the backup VPN, and how fast is failover expected to be?
questions.answer: On-premises routers prepend AS 65010 three times on prefixes advertised over the VPN. With BFD on Direct Connect, failover to the VPN completes in under 60 seconds.

sources.passage: To keep Direct Connect preferred, the on-premises routers prepend AS 65010 three times on all prefixes advertised over the VPN. With BFD on Direct Connect, failover to the VPN is expected to complete in under 60 seconds.

questions.question: What static routes are configured for the inter-region Transit Gateway peering and why?
questions.answer: Because TGW peering does not support dynamic propagation: 10.76.0.0/14 points to the peering attachment in us-east-2 and 10.64.0.0/14 points to the peering attachment in us-west-2.

sources.passage: Transit Gateway peering does not support dynamic propagation, so static routes are configured: 10.76.0.0/14 points to the peering attachment in us-east-2, and 10.64.0.0/14 points to the peering attachment in us-west-2.

questions.question: Which alarm detects Transit Gateway blackhole packet drops and what is its threshold?
questions.answer: hrl-tgw-blackhole-drops fires when PacketDropCountBlackhole is greater than 0 for 5 consecutive minutes and pages the network on-call.

sources.passage: The CloudWatch alarm hrl-tgw-blackhole-drops fires when PacketDropCountBlackhole is greater than 0 for 5 consecutive minutes and pages the network on-call.

questions.question: What is the maximum session duration for the HRL-PlatformAdmin permission set?
questions.answer: 4 hours. It is assigned only to the CPE platform team.

questions.question: What are the rotation and inactivity rules for IAM access keys?
questions.answer: Keys must be rotated at a maximum age of 90 days; credentials unused for 45 days are disabled automatically and those unused for 90 days are deleted.

sources.passage: Access keys must be rotated at a maximum age of 90 days. Credentials unused for 45 days are automatically disabled, and credentials unused for 90 days are deleted.

questions.question: What happens when a break-glass user signs in to the console?
questions.answer: The sign-in matches EventBridge rule hrl-breakglass-login, which notifies SNS topic hrl-security-critical and opens a SEV1 security incident. The password is rotated after every use.

sources.passage: Any console sign-in by a break-glass user matches the EventBridge rule hrl-breakglass-login, which notifies the SNS topic hrl-security-critical and opens a SEV1 security incident.

questions.question: Within what time must a High severity IAM Access Analyzer finding be remediated, and which analyzer produces these findings?
questions.answer: High findings must be remediated within 7 days (escalated to the Director of Cloud Platform Engineering if missed). Findings come from hrl-org-access-analyzer in the hrl-security-tooling account.

sources.passage: The organization-level IAM Access Analyzer hrl-org-access-analyzer runs in the hrl-security-tooling account

questions.question: Under what conditions can a developer create a new IAM role?
questions.answer: Only under the IAM path /app/ and only if the HRL-DeveloperBoundary permission boundary is attached to the new role.

sources.passage: Developers using the HRL-Developer permission set may create IAM roles only under the path /app/ and only if the permission boundary HRL-DeveloperBoundary is attached to the new role.

questions.question: Why should new guardrails for the Workloads/Prod OU be merged into an existing SCP?
questions.answer: AWS Organizations allows at most five SCPs attached directly to a target and Workloads/Prod already uses four of its five slots.

sources.passage: The Workloads/Prod OU currently uses four of its five SCP slots, so new controls should be merged into an existing SCP rather than attached separately.

questions.question: During throttling, how high can on-call raise reserved concurrency without CAB approval, and why is there a limit?
questions.answer: Up to 600 without CAB approval. Above 600 needs emergency CAB approval because Atlas ERP supports at most 650 concurrent connections.

questions.question: What are the rules for redriving messages from the OEP dead-letter queue?
questions.answer: Redrive only after the root cause is fixed, at a maximum of 50 messages per second; more than 10,000 messages requires Incident Commander approval; redrive must start within the 14-day DLQ retention.

sources.passage: Use the SQS console or StartMessageMoveTask with a maximum velocity of 50 messages per second. Redriving more than 10,000 messages requires approval from the Incident Commander.

questions.answer: A security group change removed the egress rule to 172.20.14.0/24 on TCP 8443, so every invocation timed out against Atlas ERP. The SEV1 outage lasted 47 minutes and 18,240 messages went to the DLQ.
